prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-02-19. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 2.29 |
| Retained earnings       | 3,431M |
| Current liabilities     | 5,712M |
| Current assets          | 13,066M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 33,867M |
| Total liabilities       | 23,079M |
| Total assets            | 57,121M |
| EBIT / operating income | 3,688M |
| Revenue                 | 6,571M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-02-19, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company exhibits a strong current ratio of 2.29 and substantial retained earnings, indicating good short-term liquidity and reinvestment. However, the debt-to-equity ratio (Total liabilities / Shareholders' equity) is high at 0.68 (23,079M / 33,867M), and the EBIT coverage of total liabilities is relatively low given the asset base, suggesting a moderate level of leverage that could be a concern for long-term solvency despite healthy current assets. The revenue to asset base is also relatively low at 11.5% (6,571M / 57,121M) and the EBIT margin is good at 56% (3,688M / 6,571M).

DECISION: A-
